oneLine: TPG and Norwest explore partial exits in a ₹400 crore deal with Neo Secondaries and Kenro Capital.

sources.title: SK Finance’s early backers eye part exits to Neo, Kenro in ₹400 crore deal

synopsis: Long-term private equity backers TPG and Norwest Venture Partners are exploring partial exits from Jaipur-based non-banking financial company SK Finance in a deal valued at ₹ 400 crore. Neo Secondaries Fund and Kenro Capital are expected to acquire the combined stake in the lender. Conversations regarding the transaction are currently underway. This comes more than a year after SK Finance shelved its plans for an initial public offering of about ₹ 2,200 crore, which had received regulatory approval. As of December 2025, Norwest, TPG, Baring Private Equity India, Evolvence and 360 ONE’s Special Opportunities Fund collectively held a 62.34% stake in the company. Emails sent to SK Finance, Norwest, and Kenro did not elicit a response, while TPG and Neo declined to comment.
